_comment_family: The other end of the same optical size, and the reason both packs
declare a full name instead of 'Texturina 18pt': the two files share
name ID 1, so the family alone names neither of them. See the note in
texturina-18pt-regular.json, which this pack is the other half of;
every word of it applies here unchanged, including why the 18pt cut
is the one shipped.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Asking for 800 or 900 on the strength of how loud a highlight
should be would invite a browser to synthesise a heavier face on top
of one that already has its own weight - and synthesised bold is the
one kind of emphasis that cannot be measured, since the smear it adds
is not in any metric the layout reads.
Two measurements say the pair sets cleanly on one line, taken at the
40px the caption is set at. Both cuts put their capitals at 28.16px -
the same 704 units of a 1000-unit em - so a picked word neither rides
above the line it is part of nor sits inside it. And the Bold runs
about five percent wider than the Regular over the same capitals,
which is worth knowing rather than worth fixing: it is wide enough to
move where a line would break if the words were re-wrapped after a
highlight was picked, and nothing re-wraps them - a caption arrives
already broken (see js/caption.js) and the user's own breaks are
theirs. It is also a real difference in colour on the page, which is
what a highlight made of weight has to be.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is

_comment_stack: The block's stack, entry for entry, and that is the correct answer
here rather than the laziness it would be next door in marydale-bold.
There the difference between block and highlight was a HAND - two
unrelated families - so the two stacks had to stay apart or the
distinction vanished with the files. Here the difference is a WEIGHT,
and weight travels in the font string beside the family rather than
inside it (see textProps in js/text.js): this face is asked for at
700 and the block's at 400, so the two may share every fallback and
still come out heavy against light.
Georgia and Times New Roman both have a real Bold on every Windows
this app runs on, so a machine that lost both files still gets a
picked word that is visibly heavier than its neighbours in the same
typeface as them - which is the whole shape of this channel's
highlight, badly drawn rather than gone.
